name: Tripura
summary_text: Tripura exhibits the country's clearest border-checkpoint pattern of profiling gender-nonconforming presentation as a suspicion trigger for foreign infiltration. In early August 2024, police reported apprehending 15 Bangladeshi nationals including seven transgender individuals in separate incidents within 24 hours; the group intercepted at the Panisagar check post numbered seven, per police reporting two transgender individuals plus others "disguised as third-gender" — the framing that trans presentation is a disguise for infiltration is explicit in the police account. In November 2024, coordinated 24-hour operations across the state detained twelve more Bangladeshi nationals, including minors and transgender people. The state shares an 856 km border with Bangladesh. These are named-state-actor operations with published counts, constituting a patterned enforcement practice directly facing any trans-presenting visitor crossing by land. The deviation from the national 0.43 is substantial (−0.12): while India has no statute criminalising trans presence, Tripura's checkpoint regime converts gender-nonconforming appearance into an independently sufficient reason for detention and deportation proceedings. Compared to West Bengal (0.34), which shares the same script but records it in fewer, more isolated incidents, Tripura's repeated 24-hour sweep operations and the explicit "disguise" framing make it the most concentrated instance of this visitor-facing harm in the country. Tripura does have a constituted transgender welfare board (one of only 12 states/UTs), but the RTI investigation found most such boards to be "rudderless" with no compliance mechanism or real power — this institutional presence does not offset active police profiling at the border.

sources.title: Tripura Police Nabs 15 Bangladeshi Nationals, Including 7 Transgenders
sources.claim_summary: Sentinel Assam report (2 Aug 2024): in the past 24 hours Tripura authorities apprehended 15 Bangladeshi nationals including seven transgender individuals in separate incidents; the first involved a bus intercepted at the Panisagar check post (North Tripura district), detainees carrying fake Aadhaar and PAN cards; state shares an 856-km porous border. Primary count for the August sweep.

sources.title: Tripura Police Arrest Seven Bangladeshi Nationals, Including Two Transgender Individuals & Four Disguised As Third-Gender - Northeast Today
sources.claim_summary: Northeast Today report (2 Aug 2024): seven Bangladeshi nationals apprehended at the Panisagar check post on the Agartala highway en route to Mumbai — per the article, two transgender individuals plus others police described as "disguised as third-gender" persons. The source of the explicit disguise framing.

sources.title: Tripura: 12 Bangladesh Nationals, Including Minors & Transgender People, Arrested
sources.claim_summary: Sentinel Assam report (9 Nov 2024): in coordinated operations across Tripura over 24 hours, twelve Bangladeshi nationals including minors and transgender people were detained; a post-midnight group of six included three transgender persons, destined for Mumbai. Establishes the pattern recurring months after the August cluster.

sources.title: Constitution of Transgender Welfare Boards/Commissions
sources.claim_summary: Press Information Bureau, Government of India (8 Dec 2021, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment): state-wise list of the 12 states/UTs that had constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under section 10(1) of the Transgender Persons Rules 2020 — Tripura included. Official record of the board's existence.

sources.title: The Reality of Transgender Welfare Boards in India: An RTI Investigation
sources.claim_summary: The Quint RTI investigation (5 Nov 2024) into state Transgender Welfare Boards: most of the 12 constituted boards lack a compliance mechanism or real power and were found leaderless or inactive — the basis for treating board existence as nominal rather than an offset to border profiling.
